idea_name: Statistical filter feature relevance for next-bar direction
mechanism: Build a binary target from TARGET_CLOSE>TARGET_OPEN, then score categorical calendar features with Chi-squared SelectKBest and continuous OHLC/lag/SMA/std features with ANOVA f_classif; keep top-k by F-score/p-value (or RFE/SFS/Lasso/RF importance) so only features with measured association to direction enter the sensor stack.
data_needed: OHLC with lags, 30DAY_SMA, 7DAY_STDDEV, DIFF_LAG1_*, DAYOFMONTH/WEEK/YEAR/MONTH; labeled next open/close
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Forex OHLC daily-style Kaggle timeseries (TARGET_OPEN/TARGET_CLOSE); MetaTrader symbols/indicators referenced generally
why_new_for_mis: Treats feature relevance itself as a sensing gate: MIS can periodically re-score which calendar and lag-vol features still associate with direction instead of freezing a static feature set.
quote: From the outputs above, we see that DAYOFYEAR has the highest Chi2 score which indicates that it is the most impactful variable on the target variable compared to the others.

idea_name: Scheduled online model refresh under non-stationary peaks
mechanism: Python client periodically pulls recent closed bars via copy_rates_from_pos, retrains CatBoost/GRU, writes ONNX (+ scaler bins) to MT5 Common\Files; EA OnTimer deletes and reloads the ONNX so predictions track distribution shifts such as instruments hitting new highs that look like outliers to stale models.
data_needed: Streaming OHLC + tick_volume from MT5; bullish/bearish label from future_close vs future_open
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD H1; GBPUSD H1; Bitcoin and NASDAQ/S&P cited as peak-seeking vs ranging forex
why_new_for_mis: Frames sensing not as a static classifier but as a timed adaptation loop when recent extremes obsolete batch-trained distributions—directly useful for MIS regime-change monitoring of model/data freshness.
quote: Unlike forex instruments which usually go up and down within specific ranges historically, instruments like NASDAQ 100, S&P 500 and others of their kind and stocks usually tends to increase and hit new peak values.

idea_name: CatBoost incremental chunk learning for streaming bars
mechanism: Split a long EURUSD H1 history into fixed chunks (e.g. 1000 bars); fit CatBoost on chunk 0, then each later chunk calls fit(..., init_model=prior.cbm) so the classifier updates from small batches without full batch retrain, then export final ONNX for live use.
data_needed: Large OHLC stream chunked chronologically with next-bar direction labels
why_new_for_mis: Gives MIS a concrete incremental-update sensor path for gradual drift without waiting for a full offline rebuild.
quote: Modern machine learning techniques like CatBoost comes with incremental learning in mind. This training method can be used for Online learning and it can help save a lot of memory when working with big data, as data can be split into small chunks which can be re-trained back to the initial model.

idea_name: GRU sequence window for next-bar direction
mechanism: StandardScaler + create_sequences with time_step=10 on OHLC/time/tick_volume; GRU classifier predicts next-bar bullish/bearish; MT5 copies last 10 closed bars, applies saved scaler mean/scale, runs ONNX softmax/binary predict.
data_needed: Ordered H1 bars with features [time, open, high, low, close, tick_volume]; sequence length 10
why_new_for_mis: Explicit short temporal receptive field as a live sequence sensor that can be hot-reloaded with the online-learning schedule.
quote: To receive the predictions from the GRU model, we have to consider the timestep value which helps Recurrent Neural Networks(RNNs) understand temporal dependencies in the data. We used a timestep value of ten(10)

idea_name: Rolling close variance and ATR range features in unified dataframe
mechanism: In MQL5 CDataFrame, insert Rolling(close,5).Var(), Pct_change(close), high-low range, ATR(14), Bollinger bands and MACD lines so the same causal feature vector used for training is rebuilt for ONNX inference on D1.
data_needed: Daily OHLC; BB(20,2), ATR(14), MACD(12,26,9); 5-day rolling variance
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD PERIOD_D1 (training ~10000 bars; live inference ~30 bars)
why_new_for_mis: Operationalizes short-horizon realized variance and ATR as first-class live sensors kept bit-identical between Python training and MQL5 deployment.
quote: Since we are working on a daily timeframe, let's add the variance of the 5 days to capture the variability patterns within a rolling 5-day period.

idea_name: LOOCV-tuned ridge fusion of multicollinear oscillators
mechanism: Standardize features; estimate betas via (X'X+λI)^−1 X'y; choose λ by leave-one-out CV minimizing MSE; feed ridge betas into linear predictor so highly correlated oscillators (Stochastic/RSI/Bears/Bulls/Volume) shrink instead of overfitting when predicting the target series.
data_needed: Oscillator/volume panel or NASDAQ_DATA.csv multivariate series; standardized design matrix
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD H1 oscillators demo; NASDAQ_DATA.csv for ridge vs OLS train/test
why_new_for_mis: Provides a sensing fusion layer that stays stable when MIS inputs are collinear technicals—λ becomes a tunable bias/variance dial for multivariate market state estimates.
quote: Ridge regression itself is a method of estimating the coefficients of a linear regression model when the independent variables are highly correlated.

idea_name: GBDT next-bar direction from OHLC geometry features
mechanism: Train LightGBM/XGBoost on [open, high, low, close, close-open, high-low, close-low, close-high] for binary next-bar class; export ONNX; on new H1 bar run predict_bin/proba and optionally threshold probability before trade.
data_needed: H1 OHLC geometry features; binary label from next close vs open
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD H1 (train CSV; tester 2023-01-01 to 2024-05-23; OOS script ~9000 bars)
why_new_for_mis: Tree-ensemble direction sensor that needs no scaling, handles missingness, and exposes class probabilities for confidence-gated MIS signals.
quote: The model was 73% accurate in out-of-sample data. This tells us our model is doing fine despite not being able to produce an upward-heading curve in the strategy tester.

mechanism: Precompute FFD weights ω_k=−ω_{k−1}(d−k+1)/k until |ω|<τ; each new closed bar take last width+1 prices (optionally log), return dot(weights, window). Tune d* offline for stationarity vs memory; deploy via indicator or embedded CFFDEngine on any applied price.
data_needed: Price series (close or other applied price); parameters d and threshold τ; optional log transform
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Any MT5 symbol/period; examples d=0.4, τ=1e-5 (width≈1457) or τ=1e-4 (width≈281); multi-feature engines with different d*
why_new_for_mis: Supplies a causal, bounded-lookback transform that keeps long memory while targeting stationarity—useful as a regime-memory sensor rather than raw integrated prices.
quote: Three properties of the FFD method make it ideal for live deployment: the weight vector is precomputed once, each observation depends on a bounded lookback window, and the computation is a single dot product.

idea_name: Causal Williams fractal S/R, breakout and trend-density sensors
mechanism: Detect n=2 (five-bar) fractal highs/lows via centered rolling extrema, measure strength vs local mean, validate, ffill rolling max/min of validated fractals as resistance/support, flag breakouts vs shifted fractal levels, then trend_strength=breakout density and trend_direction=sign(breakout balance); shift leaky columns by n before using as X.
data_needed: OHLC + external volatility (ATR); n, lookback_period, ma_period
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Scale-invariant across bar types (tick/minute/daily cited); synthetic RW used to quantify leak; general forex OHLC
why_new_for_mis: Turns structural swing geometry into leak-safe regime features (S/R distance, breakout flags, trend density) that MIS can run across timeframes with the same n.
quote: The practical value of a confirmed fractal is as a reference level: the market has already demonstrated that it rejected moves beyond that level once, so a return to the same level is a natural place to look for a repeat rejection (support/resistance) or a break of structure.

mechanism: Replace static strength threshold with threshold = volatility_threshold * (volatility / rolling_mean(volatility, 2n+1)) so fractal validity scales with current ATR vs local average, then feed validated fractals into S/R and signals.
data_needed: Fractal strength series plus aligned ATR/volatility series
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Same fractal pipeline; ATR as volatility input
why_new_for_mis: Stops over-validating spikes in high-vol regimes and under-validating in calm ones—makes structural sensors volatility-aware.
quote: Accept an optional volatility argument and scale the threshold by the ratio of current to local-average volatility: threshold = volatility_threshold * (volatility / volatility.rolling(2n+1).mean()).

idea_name: Laplace GP classifier with uncertainty-aware class probability
mechanism: Place GP prior on latent f, use logit likelihood, approximate posterior with Laplace mode/Hessian; predict mu_f* and Var(f*), then averaged π*=E[σ(f*)] via probit/numerical/MC (not just σ(E[f*])) so low-confidence (~0.51) signals can be filtered vs high-confidence (~0.60).
data_needed: Feature matrix X and binary labels y∈{+1,−1}; kernel hyperparameters optimized by NLML
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Finance rise/fall motivating example; synthetic demos deferred to Part 2; library for general binary classification
why_new_for_mis: Adds a Bayesian direction sensor whose output is a calibrated probability plus latent variance—MIS can threshold on confidence rather than hard labels.
quote: A signal with a probability of success of 0.51 (which is only slightly better than random guessing) will have much less value than a signal with a probability of 0.60. This allows the trader to set thresholds for entering a trade.

mechanism: Beginner walkthrough of FileSelectDialog/FileOpen/FileWrite plus HistorySelect loops to export trade IDs, symbols, entry/exit fields into CSV—no market regime, volatility, liquidity, or predictive sensor is constructed.
data_needed: Account deal history between start_time and end_time
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Account trade history (any symbols traded); journal CSV
why_new_for_mis: No MIS sensing idea after full read; pure language/API tutorial for journaling.
quote: In this article, we explored how to handle trade data files in MQL5 by recording both entry and exit information

series_key: the price movement model and its main provisions
idea_name: Morlet-minimizing wavelet package for oscillator extrapolation
mechanism: Model price probability amplitude as interfering faded fluctuation modes; uncertainty relation Δx·Δk ≥ 1/2 is minimized by Gaussian-modulated sinusoid (Morlet); decompose lagging oscillators into anti-symmetric wavelets and extrapolate to reduce indicator lag.
data_needed: Quote history for spectral/wavelet decomposition; oscillator series (RVI, Stochastic, MACD)
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD M30/Daily/Monthly and XAUUSD Monthly screenshots for Probabilities distribution / extrapolators
why_new_for_mis: Gives a principled wavelet basis tied to price uncertainty geometry for forecasting filtered oscillators rather than raw prices.
quote: The ratio (17) is important for practice since it provides us with the expression for the wavelet function (Morlet wavelet) allowing us to efficiently (or with the least error) decompose the price series for its extrapolation.

series_key: the price movement model and its main provisions
idea_name: Upcoming spike criterion from rising price–wavevector uncertainty product
mechanism: When the probability-density envelope becomes asymmetric into a spike, product Δx·Δk rises above the Morlet minimum; monitor the positive function built from that relation (eq. 17 in Part 2) as an early-warning criterion for internally generated spikes (vs unpredictable external jumps).
data_needed: Estimates of price uncertainty and wave-vector uncertainty / probability-density shape around the mean
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD M5 Probabilities distribution of price indicator example; general FX quotes
why_new_for_mis: Concrete change sensor: rising uncertainty product flags impending discontinuous moves caused by internal market dynamics.
quote: Thus, an increase in Δx·Δk can serve as a criterion for a possible price spike, if it is caused by internal market processes.

series_key: the price movement model and its main provisions
idea_name: Potential-well discrete price levels and jump corridors
mechanism: Evolve the price probability field with a Schrödinger-analogue equation; deep potential wells imply discrete eigen-price levels with exponential barrier penetration—observed as horizontal levels with spike transitions between them and higher uncertainty during the jump.
data_needed: Estimated potential / probability field over price; level detection from distribution indicator
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD M5 chart with marked levels and spikes via Probabilities distribution of price
why_new_for_mis: Interprets sticky price levels and inter-level spikes as eigenstates of a probabilistic field—usable as a structural regime map rather than ad hoc S/R lines.
quote: Knowing the current potential, we can easily find these price levels, between which the price moves in jumps. Practice shows that such price levels do exist.

series_key: the price movement model and its main provisions
idea_name: Reducible-price random walk around wave-field mean
mechanism: Observed Bid/Ask reductions sample the latent probability density; ticks fluctuate around the non-lagging mean set by the wave field with variance from the field uncertainty—MIS should track movement of that mean and distribution width, not every random reduction spike.
data_needed: Quote reductions across liquidity providers; estimates of mean (18) and squared uncertainty (19)
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: FX liquidity-provider / aggregator reducible Bid-Ask; general instrument quotes
why_new_for_mis: Separates noisy tick reductions from the informative mean/distribution evolution—guides volatility sensing toward field width around the mean.
quote: What is really important is a movement of the average and their distribution around it.
